planted_defects.summary: Planning horizon ends in 2051 at Alex's age 85 (Sam is 83), far short of joint-survivorship norms for a couple
The same 6.5% return is applied every single year of drawdown, so sequence-of-returns risk is invisible by construction
Spending is £42,000 in every row for 26 years with no inflation increase, while the 6.5% return is nominal — the mismatch inflates the ending balance
State Pension is taken from age 66 for both partners; for people born in 1966 and 1968 the State Pension age is 67
State Pension amount of £203.85/week is the 2023/24 rate carried in with no source or date; it has been uprated since
All withdrawals are gross-of-tax; income tax on pension drawdown beyond the tax-free portion is not modelled anywhere
The online planner's 100% success rate comes from FlexSpend that auto-cuts spending up to 25% in poor markets, so it cannot fail by construction and does not show £42,000 is sustainable
